content: Preparation H is a widely recognized brand of medications specifically formulated for the treatment of hemorrhoids. Initially, it was packaged in a tube resembling toothpaste, with a similar consistency to the latter. The manufacturer, Wyeth, also introduced a suppository form of the product, although this form has not achieved the same level of popularity as the cream. The origins of Preparation H date back to approximately 1935. The company now known as Wyeth was originally incorporated in 1926 under the name American Home Products (AHP). One of AHP's earliest notable acquisitions was a sunburn oil in 1935, which the company reformulated into Preparation H. This product subsequently became one of the most successful hemorrhoid treatments globally. In 2002, AHP officially changed its name to Wyeth. Preparation H is available in various formulations. Some are water-based gels, while others are petroleum jelly-based. The formulations range from simple moisturizers containing witch hazel, an astringent, to those with active pharmacological ingredients such as phenylephrine, pramoxine, and hydrocortisone. Certain formulations also include ingredients with less well-defined properties, such as aloe vera, shark liver oil, and yeast extract. The specific formulations available can vary by country. For example, phenylephrine, a vasoconstrictor that narrows blood vessels, is included in some versions. This ingredient is commonly used in cold medications as a decongestant, as it reduces mucus production by restricting blood flow in the sinuses. In the context of hemorrhoids, phenylephrine helps reduce the size of inflamed blood vessels. Preparation H with hydrocortisone contains only hydrocortisone as its active ingredient, typically at a 1% concentration. Additionally, a witch hazel medicated wipe is available under the Preparation H brand. The Canadian formulation of Preparation H includes a yeast extract known as BioDyne, which has been removed from the U.S. formulation. This yeast extract is believed by some to reduce wrinkles and heal dry, cracked, and irritated skin. Consequently, the Canadian version has gained a niche market in the United States as a skin cream. Despite criticism of the practice, Preparation H is occasionally recommended as part of tattoo aftercare. The rationale is that the same properties that alleviate anal irritation may also soothe the skin of a freshly tattooed area. Some individuals claim that it is less damaging to tattoos than petroleum jelly, which may pull ink from a fresh design. However, there is no scientific evidence to support these claims. For formulations containing vasoconstrictors, the narrowing of blood vessels can reduce bleeding and may help prevent the formation of scar tissue during the healing process of a tattoo. However, Dr. Jeff Herndon, an assistant professor in the Department of Medicinal Chemistry at Virginia Commonwealth University’s Medical College, has explicitly stated that Preparation H formulations containing yeast extract and shark liver oil should not be used for tattoos. Plastic surgeons have suggested that Preparation H can be applied to healing skin to alleviate itching. Scratching newly healed skin can disrupt the healing process and potentially cause damage. In the 1960s, Preparation H was marketed with the slogan, Effective even in cases of long standing. For years, there was a rumor that Preparation H was the most shoplifted item in U.S. supermarkets, as customers were reportedly embarrassed to purchase it at the cash register.
